full_judgment:
8. We have perused the impugned judgment and the evidence on record of the case. Taking us through the evidence and materials on record Mr Enayetur Rahim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is illegal and not maintainable in law. He contended that the learned Additional Sessions Judge having himself found that the prosecution has failed to prove the case against the appellants and others the order of conviction and sentence having passed on the basis of the confessional statement of the appellants, is not maintainable as those are not admissible in evidence and also not corroborated by any independent witness. He further assailed the impugned judgment submitting that the prosecution has failed to prove the manner of occurrence by cogent evidence and the prosecution evidence suffers from material contradiction and omission. He further submits that the prosecution has neither produced the Magistrate who recorded the alleged confessional statements of the appellants and another nor gave any explanation for his non-examination and in absence of his evidence the finding of the trial Court that the confessional statements of the appellants were voluntary and true is injudicious and ought not to have been relied upon. He lastly submits that the trial Court convicted the appellants and another under section 392 of the Penal Code on the basis of the aforesaid confessional statements for an occurrence and charge framed under section 395 of the Penal Code which the prosecution failed to prove and, as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. In support of his submission Mr Enayetur Rahim has referred the decision in the case between Babul alias Abdul Majid Khan and ors vs State, reported in 42 DLR (AD) 186 and another decision in the case between Shaharul Islam alias Green vs State, reported in 1 BLC 524. 

 25. The learned Additional Sessions Judge having himself found that the prosecution case was not established by cogent oral evidence of the PWs examined by the prosecution, he then turned to so- called confessional statements of the accused appellants for his safe landing for passing the order of conviction and sentence against the appellants and another and that too under section 392 of the Penal Code and not under section 395 of the Penal Code for which the appellants and another are alleged to have made their confessional statements. We have examined those confessional statements as well and find that the recording Magistrate did not properly follow the requirement of section 164 of CrPC before recording the statement of the accused under the said section and all the columns were not properly filled in by him by putting question to the accused-persons and the reply he received from them. The defence has seriously challenged the manner of recording of the so-called confessional statements as well as the genuineness and veracity of those statements. The learned Advocate for the appellants has categorically submitted that in the attending circumstances of the case and due to non-examination of the recording Magistrate the appellants have been seriously prejudiced and the said confessional statements of the appellants are not admissible in evidence. The learned Additional Sessions Judge unfortunately, passed the order of conviction and sentence entirely relying on the confessional statements allegedly made by the appellants. Although he found absolutely no oral evidence of any PWs against the appellants in support of alleged offence under section 395 of the Penal Code he passed the order of conviction and sentence under section 392, Penal Code. The learned Judge convicting the appellants on their respective confessional statements presuming under section 80 of the Evidence Act that those statements were correctly recorded by the recording Magistrate complying with the requirement of section 164 CrPC. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants seriously assailed the said finding of the trial Court as well as the order of conviction submitting that in the attending facts and circumstances of the case those statements are not admissible in evidence and cannot be treated those statements as immuned and proved under section 80 of the Evidence Act.
